title: Exponentiation of an Euler-Liar Unit
statement: Let $N>1$ be an odd natural number, and let $u$ be a unit modulo $N$ whose residue class satisfies $\left(\frac{u}{N}\right)=u^{(N-1)/2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, where the left side is the Jacobi symbol interpreted modulo $N$. Then $u^{N-1}=1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$.
hypotheses_covered: $u$ belongs to the Euler-liar subgroup, equivalently its Jacobi symbol modulo $N$ equals its $(N-1)/2$ power in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$
